title: The Byrock Story
description: A public-safe staging version of the Byrock story, focused on founder-led science, equine laminitis, PTP-102, and the path from platform evolution to disciplined development.

nodes.title: Byrock Technologies
nodes.summary: Byrock Technologies is a founder-led biotechnology company translating long-running scientific insight into practical veterinary innovation. Its lead public program is PTP-102, an investigational therapy being developed for equine laminitis. The story is not a single discovery moment; it is the result of years of work across enzyme inhibition, antibody science, laminitis biology, formulation, study design, and regulatory planning.

media.alt: Dark premium biotech cover visual with the Byrock Technologies identity, subtle cyan linework, and a connection between equine health and therapeutic science.

nodes.title: The Unmet Need in Laminitis
nodes.summary: Laminitis remains one of the most serious and feared conditions in equine medicine. It affects the tissues that support the hoof, can cause severe pain and lameness, and may progress to structural damage, long recovery periods, loss of function, or euthanasia. For owners, trainers, and veterinarians, the need is clear: better ways to intervene earlier, protect the hoof-supporting tissues, and improve the quality of evidence behind new treatment options.

media.alt: Illustrated horse profile with the hoof region highlighted in a restrained clinical infographic style.

nodes.title: The Scientific Rationale
nodes.summary: Byrock’s scientific rationale focuses on the biological cascade behind laminitis: inflammation, metalloprotease activity, oxidative stress, and damage to the lamellar structures that help suspend the coffin bone within the hoof. PTP-102 is being studied as an investigational candidate designed to intervene in these damaging pathways. The mechanism should be presented as a rational development hypothesis supported by early research, not as a final clinical conclusion.

media.alt: Simplified mechanism diagram showing inflammatory and tissue-damaging pathways involved in laminitis with an investigational intervention point.

nodes.title: From PTP-100 to PTP-102
nodes.summary: Byrock did not arrive at PTP-102 in one jump. The platform began with PTP-100, an early camelid antibody and plasma-derived laminitis concept focused on inflammatory and proteolytic drivers. It then evolved through PTP-101, a synthetic peptide approach aimed at metalloprotease inhibition. PTP-102 represents the next refinement: a methylated tirilazad program built around a synthetic nonglucocorticoid 21-aminosteroid. This sequence shows scientific progression and increasing definition, not commercial approval.

media.alt: Three-step timeline showing the evolution of the Byrock laminitis platform from PTP-100 through PTP-101 to PTP-102.

nodes.title: Research Evidence to Date
nodes.summary: The evidence story combines several strands: the earlier controlled ETCR work around PTP-100, in-vitro lamellar explant work, internal study summaries, and a 2024 peer-reviewed publication describing methylated tirilazad / PTP-102 in an oligofructose-induced laminitis model. The message should be confident but disciplined: the findings are encouraging and scientifically important, but they remain developmental and must be interpreted in light of study design, sample size, and the need for further validation.

nodes.title: Regulatory Pathway
nodes.summary: PTP-102 is investigational and is being advanced through a staged veterinary development path. The current work is about building the evidence package properly: study design, site discipline, adverse-event capture, formulation and manufacturing considerations, regulatory engagement, and a product development plan that can support the next phase. No public wording should imply approval, launch timing, or market availability before those steps are complete.

nodes.title: How the Program Is Being Studied
nodes.summary: The program is being shaped around practical veterinary evidence: appropriate horse selection, treatment timing, clinical observation, Obel lameness scoring, hoof-related assessment, safety monitoring, and follow-up over meaningful timepoints. The aim is to move from promising science to clean, defensible case and study data. Broader validation and larger, better-controlled evidence remain essential before definitive claims can be made.

nodes.title: The Team Behind Byrock
nodes.summary: Byrock is built around founder-led scientific invention supported by medical, veterinary, project-development, legal, and corporate experience. Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, anchors the story as Founder and Inventor. Dr. Daniel Shanahan-Prendergast, MD, supports medical and clinical strategy. Cormac Jones coordinates project development and partner engagement. Dr. Julio Cesar Prado, DVM, brings veterinary clinical-trials experience, while Anthony Joyce supports legal and corporate matters. Together, the team connects scientific origin, clinical translation, operational follow-through, and strategic development.

nodes.title: Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD
nodes.summary: Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, is the founder and inventor behind the Byrock technology story. His background spans microbiology, genetics, virology, antiviral development, antibody science, enzyme inhibition, and biotechnology venture creation. The evolution from PTP-100 through PTP-102 reflects a long-running scientific focus: identifying damaging biological pathways, finding ways to inhibit them, and translating that insight into practical therapeutic programs for serious unmet medical and veterinary needs.

media.alt: Founder spotlight featuring Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, with a short scientific career summary and a path from invention to platform evolution.

nodes.title: Pipeline and What Comes Next
nodes.summary: PTP-102 is Byrock’s lead public program in equine laminitis. The next chapter is disciplined execution: continued evidence generation, better-controlled clinical documentation, regulatory-pathway work, manufacturing planning, and strategic partner engagement. Any broader platform or adjacent programs should be referenced only when they are cleared for public disclosure. The public story should remain focused, ambitious, and clear: PTP-102 is a lead investigational program with meaningful work still ahead.
